excerpt: The ProofAtlas ranking Top 500 open problems in mathematics ranked by LLM-assessed importance Explore questions in mathematics, computation, and mathematical physics, with exact statements, status notes, and sources. This is a model-based assessment of mathematical importance, not an expert consensus or a forecast of which problems will be solved next. Resolved problems from earlier editions remain available with their original ranks and sources. 2 entries have conditional ranks. Each entry explains why. How the ranking works What importance means here. Each entry is a specific mathematical question. Importance considers the significance of a resolution, centrality within its field, reach across fields, scholarly and historical fame, broader recognition, and scientific or practical impact. How problems are ranked. LLMs compare pairs of problems. A reliability-weighted model combines those judgments into the ranking, with calibration across model families. The model-family weights are OpenAI 1.00, Claude 1.00, GLM 0.95, and DeepSeek 0.90. These are modeling choices, not measured probabilities of correctness. What a rank means. Nearby ranks can be uncertain. The expanded entries include available ranking ranges and comparison counts. Filtering or alphabetizing the directory preserves every problem’s rank in this edition. Diagnostics from the preceding source fit. After the reported resolutions, edition ranks were compacted without a new numerical fit. The displayed uncertainty ranges and comparison counts come from the preceding fit of 1,280 targets; the current eligible pool contains 1,122. These diagnostics were not recomputed for the smaller pool. Related and nested problems. A substantial subproblem or generalization may receive its own rank when it has independent mathematical standing.
